title: Fire from home
literal_meaning: To tuck fire into the fold at one’s waist because it is the household’s fire.
explanation: The reason offered is familiarity: the fire belongs to the house. The imagined act brings it against the body. Our reading questions treating something harmful as harmless merely because it is one’s own. The wording itself contains no explicit prohibition; this warning is our interpretation of the image.
meaning_odia: କାରଣଟି ହେଉଛି ନିଜରପଣ—ନିଆଁଟି ଘରର। କିନ୍ତୁ ତାକୁ ଅଣ୍ଟିରେ ପୂରାଇବାର କଳ୍ପନା ଦେହ ପାଖକୁ ଆଣେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ନିଜର ବୋଲି କ୍ଷତିକାରକ ଜିନିଷକୁ ନିରାପଦ ଭାବିବା ନେଇ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଅଛି। ମୂଳ କଥାରେ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ନିଷେଧ ନାହିଁ; ସତର୍କତାଟି ଏହି ଛବିରୁ ଆମର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା।
english_summary: Our reading questions the protection supposedly offered by calling a danger one’s own.
odia_summary: ନିଜର ବୋଲି ବିପଦ ଦୂର ହୁଏ କି—ଆମ ପଢ଼ାର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ସମିତିର ନିଜ ଛାପାଖାନାରୁ ଆସିଥିବା ପତ୍ରିକାରେ ଭୁଲ ରହିଗଲା। ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “ନିଜ ଲୋକଙ୍କ କାମ, ଛାଡ଼ିଦିଅ।” ସମ୍ପାଦକ ଢଗଟି ମନେ ପକାଇ କହିଲେ, “ନିଜର ବୋଲି ଭୁଲଟି ଠିକ୍ ହୋଇଯିବନି।” / A committee newsletter contains an error. Someone says to overlook it because their own printer made it. The editor recalls the saying: “Being ours does not make the mistake right.” This exchange is invented.
cultural_context: The entry also lists family secrets as a separate sense. It supplies no domestic incident or family-abuse gloss for the quotation. The publication example is editorial, not collected usage.
